title: Dative: Exceptions & Edge Cases
titleRussian: Дательный падеж: исключения и особые случаи
description: The dative-form exceptions that sit outside the seven regular lessons: 3rd-declension feminine nouns ending in -ь (мать → ма́тери, дочь → до́чери, тетра́дь → тетра́ди) with the мать / дочь stem extension, the -мя neuters (вре́мя → вре́мени, и́мя → и́мени), and the small set of plurale-tantum dative forms (часа́м, деньга́м, очка́м) at recognition level.
descriptionRussian: Особые формы дательного падежа, которые остаются за рамками семи основных уроков: женский род 3-го склонения на -ь (мать → ма́тери, дочь → до́чери, тетра́дь → тетра́ди) с расширением основы у мать / дочь, средний род на -мя (вре́мя → вре́мени, и́мя → и́мени) и небольшая группа pluralia tantum в дательном падеже (часа́м, деньга́м, очка́м) на узнавание.
intro: The same small cast of difficult words turns up here that turned up in the genitive: the soft-sign feminines, мать and дочь with their extra syllable, and the -мя neuters. Learning them once in one case does most of the work for the next, because they misbehave the same way each time. There is also one more preposition here that takes the dative.
rules: Class 1 - 3rd-declension feminine nouns ending in -ь take dative -и (NOT -е): тетра́дь → тетра́ди; ночь → но́чи; крова́ть → крова́ти; пло́щадь → пло́щади; жизнь → жи́зни; о́сень → о́сени; ло́шадь → ло́шади. Compare with regular feminine кни́га → кни́ге, ма́ма → ма́ме.

Stem extension on мать and дочь. These two 3rd-decl feminines insert -ер- before every oblique ending. Dative: мать → ма́тери; дочь → до́чери. The same stem carries through gen ма́тери, instr ма́терью, prep о ма́тери. No other feminine noun does this.

Class 2, the -мя neuters. A closed set of neuters in -мя (вре́мя, и́мя, пле́мя, се́мя, пла́мя, зна́мя, бре́мя, те́мя, стре́мя, вы́мя) inserts -ен- before any oblique ending. Dative: вре́мя → вре́мени; и́мя → и́мени; пле́мя → пле́мени. They are neuter (despite looking feminine) and decline as a unit; the dative is identical to the genitive (-ени).

Class 3 - plurale tantum in the dative takes the regular plural ending -ам / -ям: часа́м, деньга́м, но́жницам, очка́м, су́ткам. At A2 this is mainly recognition; the full plural-cases system belongs to `b1-plural-cases-mastery`.

Map the trigger to the class. The dative TRIGGERS (помога́ть, звони́ть, дать, нра́виться, age, state predicates, к) work exactly the same way on the exception classes as on regular nouns. Only the form on the noun changes.

One more dative trigger to know here: the preposition по, meaning 'by / according to / along', also takes the dative - по и́мени means 'by name'. Like к, it just sets the case; the exception form on the noun is the same.
examples: Ма́ша помога́ет ма́тери. (Masha helps her mother.) мать → ма́тери, 3rd-decl + stem extension (Class 1).
Анто́н звони́т до́чери. (Anton calls his daughter.) дочь → до́чери, 3rd-decl + stem extension (Class 1).
Ма́ша ра́да но́вой тетра́ди. (Masha is pleased with the new notebook.) тетра́дь → тетра́ди, 3rd-decl regular, no stem extension (Class 1).
К э́тому вре́мени Ма́ша уже́ зако́нчит рабо́ту. (By this time Masha will have already finished work.) вре́мя → вре́мени, -мя neuter (Class 2).
По и́мени мы её сра́зу узна́ли. (We recognised her immediately by her name.) и́мя → и́мени, -мя neuter (Class 2).
К очка́м Ма́ши прикре́плена цепо́чка. (A chain is attached to Masha's glasses.) очки́ → очка́м, plurale tantum dative (Class 3).

cells: the -е ending you learned in L1

rows.label: Regular fem -я

items.promptEnglish: Masha calls her mother every day.
items.hint: Звони́ть takes the dative. Мать is 3rd-decl with the stem extension.
items.explanation: Звони́ть triggers the dative. Мать is 3rd-decl feminine; the dative ending is -и (not -е). It also inserts -ер- into the stem before any oblique ending: мать → ма́тери.

items.promptEnglish: By this time everything will be ready.
items.hint: К + dative. Вре́мя is a -мя neuter; what does it insert?
items.explanation: К takes the dative. Вре́мя belongs to the small closed -мя neuter class that inserts -ен- before any oblique ending: вре́мя → вре́мени.

items.promptEnglish: Masha is pleased with the new notebook.
items.hint: Рад / ра́да takes the dative. Тетра́дь is 3rd-decl regular (no stem extension).
items.explanation: Рад / ра́да + dative ('pleased with X' / 'glad of X') is one of the short-adjective dative triggers. Тетра́дь is 3rd-decl feminine: the dative ending is -и, no stem extension.

items.promptEnglish: The teacher helps her daughter with the homework.
items.hint: Помога́ть takes the dative. Дочь patterns with мать.
items.explanation: Помога́ть triggers the dative. Дочь is 3rd-decl feminine with the same stem extension as мать: дочь → до́чери (-ер- + -и).

items.promptEnglish: The boy walked up to the old banner.
items.hint: К + dative. Зна́мя is one of the -мя neuters.
items.explanation: К takes the dative. Зна́мя belongs to the -мя neuter class and follows the same pattern as вре́мя and и́мя: insert -ен-, then add the regular ending. The dative of зна́мя is зна́мени.

items.promptEnglish: We recognised her immediately by her name.
items.hint: По + dative. И́мя is a -мя neuter.
items.explanation: По 'by / according to' takes the dative. И́мя is a -мя neuter: insert -ен-, then the ending: и́мя → и́мени. The phrase по и́мени ('by name') is the most common dative use of this word and worth memorising as a chunk.

items.promptEnglish: A thin chain is attached to Masha's glasses.
items.hint: К + dative. Очки́ is a plural-only noun; the dative plural ending is -ам.
items.explanation: К takes the dative. Очки́ exists only in the plural, so the dative is the regular plural dative ending -ам: очка́м.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is glad about the new bed.
errorCorrection.explanation: Крова́ть is a 3rd-declension feminine noun (soft -ь), so its dative ending is -и, not -е: крова́ти. Крова́те is the trap that applies the regular feminine -е rule to a 3rd-declension noun.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: You must not go near the flame.
errorCorrection.explanation: Пла́мя belongs to the closed class of -мя neuters, which insert -ен- before any oblique ending: пла́мя → пла́мени. The trigger к governs the dative. Пла́мю applies a regular soft ending without the -ен- extension.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: By nightfall everything will be ready.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ночь is a 3rd-declension feminine, so its dative ending is -и: к но́чи ('by nightfall'). Но́че applies the regular feminine -е rule to a noun that does not follow it.

This is a trick: тетра́дь here is the SUBJECT of нра́вится (the thing Masha likes), so it is the nominative тетра́дь, not a dative. The dative belongs to Ма́ше (the liker). Тетра́де does not exist as any form. The adjective но́вая is nominative too, confirming the subject.

errorCorrection.sentence: Ма́ша подошла́ к крова́те и се́ла.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha walked up to the bed and sat down.
errorCorrection.explanation: Крова́ть is a 3rd-declension feminine noun (ending in soft -ь), so its dative ending is -и, not -е: к крова́ти. Крова́те applies the regular feminine -е rule (from ма́ма → ма́ме) to a noun that does not take it; 3rd-declension feminines never take -е.

errorCorrection.sentence: На выходны́е Ма́ша е́дет к роди́тели.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: For the weekend Masha is going to her parents'.
errorCorrection.explanation: К governs the dative, and in the plural the dative ending is -ам / -ям for every gender: роди́тели → роди́телям. The bare nominative роди́тели can only be a subject. After к, the plural target takes -ям: к роди́телям.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The girl gave sugar to the horse.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ло́шадь is a 3rd-declension feminine noun (soft -ь), so the dative recipient takes -и, not -е: дать кому → ло́шади. Дать puts the recipient (the horse) in the dative and the thing given (са́хар) in the accusative. Ло́шаде wrongly applies the regular feminine -е rule; 3rd-declension feminines always take -и.

errorCorrection.sentence: Учи́тель обраща́ется к ребёнку по и́мю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The teacher addresses the child by name.
errorCorrection.explanation: И́мя belongs to the closed class of -мя neuters, which insert -ен- before any oblique ending: и́мя → и́мени. The trigger по ('by') governs the dative, so the phrase по и́мени means 'by name'. И́мю applies the regular neuter -ю rule that this class does not follow.

minimalPairs.explanation: Мать is 3rd-decl feminine. The dative ending is -и (not -е). The stem extension -ер- is inserted before -и: ма́тери. *Ма́тере is the most common learner trap form; it does not exist.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is pleased with the new notebook.
minimalPairs.explanation: Рад / ра́да + dative. Тетра́дь is 3rd-decl feminine (no stem extension) and takes -и in the dative: тетра́ди. *Тетра́де applies the regular feminine -е rule (книга → книге) to a noun that does not follow it.

patternRecognition.question: Why is ма́тери the form here, not ма́тере?
options: 3rd-declension feminines take -и in the dative; мать adds the -ер- stem extension.
Ма́тери is the genitive form used after пи́шет.
patternRecognition.answer: 3rd-declension feminines take -и in the dative; мать adds the -ер- stem extension.
patternRecognition.explanation: Two rules combine. (1) 3rd-decl feminine nouns (those ending in -ь) take -и in the dative, not -е. (2) Мать and дочь additionally insert -ер- before any oblique ending. So the dative is stem ма́тер- + ending -и = ма́тери. The 'feminines take -е' rule applies only to the -а / -я class.

patternRecognition.question: Which class of nouns does вре́мени belong to?
patternRecognition.explanation: Вре́мя is a -мя neuter. The class inserts -ен- before any oblique ending: вре́мени, и́мени, пле́мени. The closed list is small (about ten nouns total), all neuter, all following the same pattern.

patternRecognition.question: Why is Ма́ше in the dative here?
options: It is the recipient of a verb of giving.
It is the experiencer in the age construction (Маше двадцать пять лет).
patternRecognition.answer: It is the experiencer in the age construction (Маше двадцать пять лет).
patternRecognition.explanation: Ма́ша is regular feminine -а, so the dative is ма́ме-style: ма́ше. The trigger here is the age construction from L4: the person whose age is being stated goes into the dative. This confirms that the dative TRIGGERS work the same way on regular and exceptional nouns - only the form on the noun changes.

patternRecognition.question: What is going on with очка́м?
options: It is gen sg of a regular masculine.
It is dat pl of a plural-only noun (очки́).
It is dat sg of a regular feminine.
It is gen pl of a regular neuter.
patternRecognition.answer: It is dat pl of a plural-only noun (очки́).
patternRecognition.explanation: Очки́ exists only in the plural. К takes the dative, so очки́ shifts to the dative plural with the regular -ам ending: очка́м. The full plural-cases system is taught in the b1-plural-cases-mastery track; here it is recognition only.

reviewVocab.definition: the small class of feminine nouns ending in soft -ь (тетра́дь, ночь, мать, дочь, крова́ть, пло́щадь, жизнь, о́сень, ло́шадь). In the dative they take -и, not -е.
reviewVocab.example: Маша помогает матери. Маша рада новой тетради.

reviewVocab.definition: the stem extension -ер- that мать and дочь insert before any oblique ending: ма́тери, до́чери (dat / gen / prep), ма́терью, до́черью (instr). No other feminine noun does this.
reviewVocab.example: Антон звонит дочери. Маша пишет матери письмо.

reviewVocab.definition: the closed neuter class ending in -мя (вре́мя, и́мя, пле́мя, се́мя, пла́мя, зна́мя, бре́мя, те́мя, стре́мя, вы́мя). They insert -ен- before any oblique ending: вре́мени, и́мени, пле́мени. The dative is identical to the genitive (-ени).
reviewVocab.example: По имени мы её узнали. К этому времени всё будет готово.

reviewVocab.definition: nouns with no singular (часы́, де́ньги, но́жницы, очки́, су́тки, кани́кулы, штаны́, духи́) take the regular plural dative ending -ам / -ям when a dative trigger pulls on them: часа́м, деньга́м, очка́м, су́ткам. At A2 this is recognition material; the full plural-cases system is taught at B1.
